## seqeron 0.17.0

**Cluster snapshots and bounded history.** With a `<snapshots>` policy, the leader starts a snapshot round when the
policy's time or `bytes` threshold is reached, or on `clusterctl request-snapshot`. Every member writes the
Sequencer's state (schema 216, `doc/snapshot.md` §10.2) and publishes the round's marker. A restarted member restores
that state, starts each queue again at the cut, and re-emits the marker as its first frame, so its recovery time and
its archive no longer grow with the history. A member's Replayer purges its queue recordings below the newest cut
every co-located application has confirmed (`restart-safe.log`), a gateway host's Replayer does the same for the
queues it relays, and `clusterctl trim-log` trims the Raft log. A cluster with no policy takes no cluster snapshots,
as before, and recovers by a full-log replay.

**A hardened replay path.** A replay that ends past a hole in its history resumes at its last dispatched frame, a
resent request is answered with the replay already running, and a cut search the archive stalls on no longer blocks
the Replayer's duty cycle. All three client tiers follow case for case.

**System tests.** The end-to-end harnesses are JUnit 6 tests that launch real child JVMs and Docker containers, and
read each member's state from its counters rather than its log. The bash harnesses they replace are deleted, apart from
the C++ and C# client ones.

A cluster upgrades together: members, gateway hosts and clients, with the archives and Raft logs purged (spec **V-3**).

### Breaking changes

- **Snapshot listeners, in every language:** `onRestore` takes the `formatVersion` of the file it reads (C#
  `OnRestore`), as does `SnapshotRestoreHandler.onSnapshotRecord`. `SnapshotListener` gains `supportsFormatVersion`,
  by default the build's own format; a format the listener refuses still fences with `SNAPSHOT_UNRESTORABLE`. A
  format change is still a coordinated upgrade (`doc/upgrades.md`).
- **A queue need not start at `groupSeqNo` 1.** A member restarted from a cluster snapshot starts its queue at the
  cut, so a consumer of a member's queue must be able to restart from a snapshot file, which only an `Application` or
  `Gateway` writes. A plain `ClusterProbe follow` cannot follow such a member. A first frame that is not
  `groupSeqNo` 1 on a walk from the start is a latched fault in every language, where Java and C# stopped silently
  and C++ aborted.
- **Wire, schema 210:** `SnapshotPolicyRegistered` carries `bytes` (int64, id 20061), the sequenced bytes between
  rounds. It needs a purged archive (spec **V-3**).
- **Wire, schema 212:** `SnapshotRound`, `SnapshotJoined` and `SnapshotConfirmed` (templates 11 to 13) carry the
  node-local snapshot signals between a node's Replayer and its applications, and `ReplayRequest` carries
  `cutClusterSeqNo`, which a restore sets. The Replayer finds the cut frame in the recording, from a kept cut or by
  reading from the file's hint or the recording's start.
- **New schema 216:** the Sequencer's snapshot.
- **Topology document:** `<snapshots>` takes a `bytes` attribute (default 0, off), and every row under `<snapshots>`
  must say `snapshot="true"`.
- **Snapshot files:** the store keeps the two newest confirmed files (was one), and a restore checks the chosen file
  against its trailer before the listener sees any of it, so a damaged file gives way to the older one, or with
  none to a walk.
- **Queue stall timeout:** 5 s by default (was 1 s) for the sequencer and a gateway host's relay, set by
  `sequencer.queueStallTimeoutMs` and `replayer.queueStallTimeoutMs`, with a minimum of 1000 (`doc/ops.md`).
- **`ReplayerStreamReceiver`:** C++ gains `queueFaults`, and C++ and C# gain `controlFaults` and `replayFaults`, as
  Java has. `replayFaults` takes the position each frame starts at.
- **C++ `ClusterStreamClient`** replays from `NULL_POSITION`, the recording's own start, which a restart at a cut or
  a purge moves off 0.

### Fixed

- **`SnapshotConfirmed` was sent before the snapshot file was durable**, and also when the write had failed. The
  Replayer takes it as the file being durable under its name, so it could mark a cut restart-safe and purge the queue
  below it while the application held no file for that round. The store records the newest durable round, and
  `SnapshotTaker` confirms only once its pending round has reached it, in Java, C++ and C#.
- **A replay that reached its bound past a hole reported the client caught up** short of the queue's tip, because the
  image's position advances over fragments the client dropped. The client now requests a resume from the last frame
  it dispatched, paced by the resend timer. A recording that kept its hole had given every resume the same one, at
  about 45 replays a second.
- **A resend started a second replay.** It keeps its `requestId` and is answered with the running replay (**R-1**),
  in all three clients.
- **A walk that stalled after dispatching a frame** started again from the recording's start. It resumes at its last
  frame.
- **A cut search the archive stalled on blocked the Replayer's duty cycle.** It returns `STALLED` after 2 s without
  progress; a stalled search from a hint falls back to the recording's start.
- **A replay with no active recording or no tip** is no longer added to the pending list, and a stalled replay frees
  its slot.
- **The Replayer's timers** run on a monotonic clock.
- **`isCaughtUp` clears while the client is evicted from its queue**, and `poll` reads the replay image before the
  stall watchdog.
- **An idle strategy backed off between a restore's 1,024-record chunks.** A restore's records now count as work.
- **A relay whose members had all purged past the next frame it needed cycled through them.** It stops with a fatal.
- **The trim fence** that stops a start from replaying a trimmed log whole is read from the first term's recording
  start in the archive catalog, not from a line in `restart-safe.log`, so a rebuilt member or a lost file keeps it.

### New

- **`clusterctl trim-log`** keeps the two newest restart-safe snapshots and the Raft log from the older one, and
  purges older snapshot recordings. `--dry-run` prints what a run would purge and purges nothing.
- **A gateway host purges its relayed queue recordings** below confirmed cuts (`doc/snapshot.md` §10.6). Gateways
  answer `SnapshotRound` with `SnapshotJoined` and `SnapshotConfirmed` in Java, C++ and C#.
- **`FaultableReplayer`**, with `SequencerServer.launch`, `ReplayerServer.launch` and
  `ReplayerServer.launchGatewayHost` taking a wrapper over the member's `AeronReplayer`, wraps a Replayer to back-pressure the control stream, read no requests, start a replay
  slowly or not at all, or freeze or end replay progress, for the integration suite.
- **A system-test suite**, `:seqeron-service:systemTest`, and `:seqeron-service:networkFaultTest` for the tests that
  need Docker and [faulteron](https://github.com/FredrikJDahlberg/faulteron). Members, probes and `clusterctl` run
  as child JVMs, a kill is a process's death, and `ChaosTest` replays its fault sequence from a printed `SEED`.
  CI runs them as `java system`, `chaos`, `docker failover` and `network faults`.
- **Integration tests** for a stalled gateway-host Replayer, a relay left behind by member purging, a clock step, and
  a paused walk.
- **A C# `SnapshotApp` example**, restored from a round it confirmed in `csharp-client-test.sh`.
- **`doc/fault-tolerance.md` §1.2** explains the two kinds of loss a producer sees across a leader kill. A leader that
  dies ends no egress, so a producer offers into its publication's term window until `NewLeader` discards what it
  holds. The failover harnesses now `SIGKILL` the leader so every run takes that path.

### Upgrading

1. Stop every member, gateway host and client, and purge each member's and gateway host's archive and Raft log
   (`purgelog.sh`). Delete every instance's snapshot files.
2. Upgrade everything together: members, gateway hosts and clients.
3. In application code: implement `onRestore(…, formatVersion)` and, if the application reads an older format,
   `supportsFormatVersion`.
4. To bound history, add a `<snapshots>` policy to the topology document with `snapshot="true"` on each row beneath
   it, and `bytes` if a size threshold is wanted. Every consumer of a member's queue must then restart from a snapshot
   file. Run `clusterctl trim-log --dry-run` before the first `trim-log`.
5. Check any override of the queue stall timeout against the new 5 s default (`doc/ops.md`).
